name: SEC EDGAR (Electronic Data Gathering, Analysis, and Retrieval)
operator: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), Division of Economic and Risk Analysis / Office of Information Technology
website: https://www.sec.gov/edgar ; full-text search UI: https://efts.sec.gov/LATEST/search-index (API) and https://www.sec.gov/edgar/search/
region_main: United States. CONFIRMED: EDGAR is the mandatory electronic filing system for issuers registered with the SEC. Scope = US-LISTED / SEC-REGISTERED issuers, NOT US-located deals. The filings themselves disclose acquisitions of targets ANYWHERE in the world (including Japan and the rest of Asia), so EDGAR is effectively a global M&A disclosure source filtered by 'the acquirer (or target) is an SEC registrant'.
region_surroundings: CONFIRMED counts, all measured 2026-09-03 by direct API/index queries: (a) 10,391 companies carry a ticker in https://www.sec.gov/files/company_tickers.json (i.e. exchange-listed registrants); 10,390 rows in company_tickers_exchange.json. (b) 1,057,621 lines in https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/cik-lookup-data.txt = every entity ever assigned a CIK (includes individuals filing Forms 3/4, funds, ABS trusts, subsidiaries) - NOT a company count. (c) From the 2025 quarterly form indexes (full-index/2025/QTR1-4/form.idx): 5,209 unique CIKs filed a 10-K (US domestic reporting companies), 988 unique CIKs filed a 20-F, 141 filed a 40-F (Canadian MJDS), 1,226 filed a 6-K. So foreign private issuers (FPIs) number roughly 1,100-1,250 active filers. (d) Asia exposure - CONFIRMED: 1,036 EDGAR filers carry a Japan business address (browse-edgar State=M0, all filer types, counted by pagination). EDGAR country codes CONFIRMED by submissions API: M0=Japan (Toyota Motor Corp, Sony Group Corp), U0=Singapore (Sea Ltd), K3=Hong Kong, E9=Cayman Islands (Sea Ltd state of incorporation). (e) 2025 20-F DOCUMENT counts by business-location code from the full-text-search biz_states_filter aggregation (documents, not filers; bucket list truncated to top 30; three buckets sat at exactly 100 so treat as approximate - INFERRED): F4 China 1,708; L3 (Israel, INFERRED) 594; K3 Hong Kong 432; U0 Singapore 401; X0 United Kingdom 400; M0 Japan ~100; F5 Taiwan ~92; K7 India ~57; M5 South Korea ~49. Conclusion: Greater China + Hong Kong dominate the Asian FPI population; Japan-headquartered SEC registrants are few (Toyota, Sony, Honda, Mitsubishi UFJ, Sumitomo Mitsui, Mizuho, Nomura, Orix, Canon-class names) but their 20-F/6-K filings do disclose Japanese and cross-border M&A. (f) NOT CONFIRMED: the SEC's own per-country FPI list is stale and PDF-only - https://www.sec.gov/divisions/corpfin/internatl/companies.shtml is 'as of December 31, 2015' with PDF reports (Alphabetical Listing, Geographic Listing by Country of Incorporation, Market Summary, Summary Information Based on Country of Incorporation); the newer staff-guidance URL returns HTTP 404.

api_access: FREE, NO AUTH. CONFIRMED endpoints and behaviour (all tested live 2026-09-03): (1) Submissions API - https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK##########.json (10-digit zero-padded CIK). Top-level keys: cik, entityType, sic, sicDescription, ownerOrg, insiderTransactionForOwnerExists, insiderTransactionForIssuerExists, name, tickers, exchanges, ein, lei, description, website, investorWebsite, category, fiscalYearEnd, stateOfIncorporation, stateOfIncorporationDescription, addresses, phone, flags, formerNames, filings. filings.recent holds parallel arrays: accessionNumber, filingDate, reportDate, acceptanceDateTime, act, form, fileNumber, filmNumber, items, core_type, size, isXBRL, isInlineXBRL, isXBRLNumeric, primaryDocument, primaryDocDescription. CRITICAL FOR M&A: the 'items' array gives 8-K item codes directly (verified: Apple 8-K of 2026-07-30 -> items '2.02,9.01'), so 8-Ks can be filtered by Item 1.01 / 2.01 / 5.01 with no document parsing. filings.recent holds the most recent ~1,000 filings (1,001 for Apple); older history is in filings.files[] paginated JSON (Apple: CIK0000320193-submissions-001.json, filingCount 1244, filingFrom 1994-01-26 to 2015-07-19) - so full filing history per CIK is available. (2) Company Facts - https://data.sec.gov/api/xbrl/companyfacts/CIK##########.json. (3) Company Concept - https://data.sec.gov/api/xbrl/companyconcept/CIK##########/{taxonomy}/{concept}.json. (4) Frames - https://data.sec.gov/api/xbrl/frames/{taxonomy}/{concept}/{units}/{period}.json, e.g. .../us-gaap/BusinessCombinationConsiderationTransferred1/USD/CY2024.json returns keys taxonomy, tag, ccp, uom, label, description, pts, data[] with {accn, cik, entityName, loc, start, end, val}. Measured CY2024 datapoint counts: PaymentsToAcquireBusinessesNetOfCashAcquired 1,600; BusinessAcquisitionsProFormaRevenue 239; BusinessCombinationConsiderationTransferred1 88. (Tags BusinessCombinationConsiderationTransferred and BusinessCombinationRecognizedIdentifiableAssetsAcquiredAndLiabilitiesAssumedNet return NoSuchKey for CY2024 - frames needs the exact tag name and an exactly-matching period.) (5) FULL-TEXT SEARCH API - https://efts.sec.gov/LATEST/search-index?q=...&forms=...&startdt=YYYY-MM-DD&enddt=YYYY-MM-DD&ciks=##########&from=N&dateRange=custom. CONFIRMED live: returns OpenSearch/Elasticsearch JSON; hits.total.value with relation 'eq' or 'gte'; 100 hits per page; each hit has _id (accession:filename), _index 'edgar_file', _score and _source {ciks, period_ending, file_num, display_names, xsl, sequence, root_forms, file_date, biz_states, sics, form, adsh, film_num, biz_locations, file_type, file_description, inc_states, items}. Aggregations returned: entity_filter (top 30 entities), sic_filter (top 30), biz_states_filter (top 30), form_filter (exact document totals per root form). forms accepts a comma-separated list (tested forms=8-K,S-4,DEFM14A -> form_filter buckets 8-K 594, S-4 110, DEFM14A 19). ciks works (tested ciks=0000320193 -> 489 hits, only Apple). Phrase search with %22...%22, boolean AND (implied)/OR/NOT, NEAR(n), trailing-stem wildcard gas*. HARD PAGINATION CAP: from=10000 returns 'Result window is too large, from + size must be less than or equal to: [10000] but was [10100]' - i.e. max 10,000 retrievable hits per query, so backfills must be sliced by form type x narrow date window. Unsupported params behave badly: items=2.01 and locationCodes=J3 both return HTTP 500; locationCode=J3 is silently IGNORED (returned Brazilian/UK/Greek issuers) - do NOT rely on a location filter, post-filter on _source.biz_states instead. Stopword-only queries (q=%22the%22) error. (6) Archives - https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/{cik}/{accession-no-dashes}/ with index.json listing every file, {accession}-index-headers.html and {accession}.txt carrying the SGML header. CONFIRMED: the SGML header exposes 'CONFORMED SUBMISSION TYPE:', 'FILED AS OF DATE:' and human-readable 'ITEM INFORMATION:' lines (verified: 'Results of Operations and Financial Condition', 'Financial Statements and Exhibits') in a ~6 KB fetch - a cheap item-level filter. (7) Indexes - https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/full-index/{YYYY}/{QTRn}/{company,form,master,xbrl}.idx and https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/daily-index/{YYYY}/{QTRn}/form.YYYYMMDD.idx (plus index.json for machine listing). RATE LIMITS - CONFIRMED: 'Current maximum: 10 requests per second'; SEC reserves the right to change it. Required header: 'User-Agent: Sample Company Name AdminContact@<sample company domain>.com'; Accept-Encoding: gzip, deflate and Host also recommended. Botnets/undeclared crawlers get blocked. data.sec.gov does NOT support CORS (so no browser-side calls from a Salesforce Lightning component - must proxy server-side/Apex).
archive_window: CONFIRMED per dataset: (a) Filing documents / quarterly full-index: 1993 to 2026 - directory listing of https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/full-index/ shows year folders 1993 through 2026 (34 years). (b) Daily index: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/daily-index/index.json lists year folders 1994 through 2026 (37 items incl. bulkdata, xbrl, sitemaps). (c) Electronic filing was phased in 1993-1996 (mandated for all domestic registrants by 1996) - INFERRED: pre-1996 coverage is partial and pre-1993 is paper-only, so any deal history before ~1996 is incomplete on EDGAR and before 1993 absent. (d) FULL-TEXT SEARCH: 2001-01-01 to present. CONFIRMED twice - FAQ says 'search the full text of all EDGAR filings submitted electronically since 2001', and a live query 'merger agreement' over 1994-01-01..2000-12-31 returned only 30 hits vs 10,000+ for 2001 alone; earliest hit in a 2001 query was 2001-01-08. (e) XBRL companyfacts/companyconcept/frames: 2009 onward (XBRL phase-in from 2009); CONFIRMED the XBRL APIs cover forms 10-Q, 10-K, 8-K, 20-F, 40-F, 6-K and variants. (f) Financial Statement Data Sets: 2009 Q1 to present, quarterly. (g) Submissions API: entire filing history per CIK (recent 1,000 inline + older paginated files; Apple back to 1994-01-26).
data_types: Primary M&A-relevant filing types with CONFIRMED 2025 volumes counted from full-index/2025/QTR1-4/form.idx (filings / unique CIKs): 8-K 67,651 / 5,476. 10-K 6,690 / 5,209. 20-F 1,078 / 988. 6-K 27,506 / 1,226. 40-F 143 / 141. S-4 391 / 295. F-4 73 / 63. SCHEDULE 13D 2,230 / 1,524 plus SCHEDULE 13D/A 9,044 / 2,923 (13D family total 11,274 - note EDGAR now labels these 'SCHEDULE 13D', not the legacy 'SC 13D'). SCHEDULE 13G 15,640 / 4,303 plus SCHEDULE 13G/A 33,420 / 5,396 (49,060 total). SC TO-T 107 / 97. SC 14D9 55 / 51. DEFM14A 235 / 230. Form 425 6,330 / 567. Form 15-12G 448 / 430 (deregistration - the tail-end marker of a completed take-private/merger). Content by form: 8-K Item 1.01 'Entry into a Material Definitive Agreement' = signing of the SPA/merger agreement; Item 1.02 'Termination of a Material Definitive Agreement' = deal break; Item 2.01 'Completion of Acquisition or Disposition of Assets' = closing; Item 5.01 'Changes in Control of Registrant'; Item 8.01 'Other Events' (catch-all often used for LOIs/updates); Item 9.01 'Financial Statements and Exhibits' carries the acquiree audited financials and pro formas. Item titles CONFIRMED verbatim by full-text-search hit counts on the exact phrases (2025, 8-K only): 'Entry into a Material Definitive Agreement' 10,000+ documents, 'Completion of Acquisition or Disposition of Assets' 1,107, 'Termination of a Material Definitive Agreement' 1,232, 'Changes in Control of Registrant' 348. S-4 / F-4 = registration statement for shares issued as merger consideration, contains the full merger background, fairness opinion, financial projections; DEFM14A / PREM14A = definitive/preliminary merger proxy with 'Background of the Merger', 'Reasons for the Merger', 'Opinion of Financial Advisor', per-share price; SC TO-T (third-party tender offer) / SC TO-I (issuer self-tender) / SC 14D9 (target board recommendation); SCHEDULE 13D = >5% stake with control intent, Item 4 'Purpose of Transaction' is where strategic/activist intent is stated, SCHEDULE 13G = passive >5%; Form 425 = written merger communications (press releases, investor decks) filed under Rule 425; Form 10-12B = spin-off/carve-out registration; 10-K/10-Q ASC 805 business-combination footnote = purchase price allocation, consideration transferred, goodwill, pro forma revenue/earnings; 6-K = FPI interim reports (M&A press releases from Japanese/Chinese issuers arrive here).
formats: CONFIRMED: primary documents are HTML (.htm) and, for older filings, plain text (.txt); the complete submission is also available as one concatenated SGML .txt. Financial statements from 2009 onward are XBRL / inline-XBRL (isXBRL, isInlineXBRL, isXBRLNumeric flags in the submissions API) and are re-served as JSON through the XBRL APIs. All REST APIs return JSON. Exhibits are separate documents typed in the full-text-search _source.file_type field - CONFIRMED distribution from a live 'Agreement and Plan of Merger' 8-K query (first 100 hits): 8-K 76, EX-99.1 8, 8-K/A 6, EX-2.1 5, EX-2.3 1, EX-10.1 1, EX-10.2 1, EX-3.1 1, EX-99.7 1. So EX-2.1 = the merger/purchase agreement itself and EX-99.1 = the press release (where headline deal value usually lives) are directly addressable by file_type. Some exhibits are PDF (graphics, investor presentations). Bulk data as ZIP (submissions.zip, companyfacts.zip) and ZIP-of-TSV (Financial Statement Data Sets: sub.txt, num.txt, tag.txt, pre.txt). Sample sizes CONFIRMED: an Apple 8-K submission totals 417,360 bytes but its primary document is only 38,350 bytes; the {accession}-index-headers.html header file is 5,945 bytes.
update_frequency: CONFIRMED: EDGAR accepts filings Mon-Fri 06:00-22:00 ET; submissions after 17:30 ET roll into the next business day's index. Submissions API delay 'typically under 1 second' after dissemination; XBRL APIs 'typically under 1 minute'. Bulk ZIPs are rebuilt nightly at approximately 03:00 ET (observed Last-Modified 2026-09-03 05:07-05:14 UTC). Daily index files appear nightly starting ~22:00 ET (form.20260902.idx present on 2026-09-03). Quarterly full-index and Financial Statement Data Sets: quarterly. Full-text search index: near-real-time (a query restricted to 2026-08-01..2026-08-31 returned current filings).
limitations: CONFIRMED / structural: (1) Universe is limited to SEC registrants - a purely private Japanese buyer acquiring a private Japanese target never appears. EDGAR only sees a deal if a US-registered issuer is the acquirer, the target, or a >5% holder. (2) No structured deal-value field anywhere in EDGAR. Consideration is prose in the 8-K body or, most often, in the EX-99.1 press release; XBRL only captures it after the fact and sparsely (only 88 companies tagged BusinessCombinationConsiderationTransferred1 for CY2024, 1,600 tagged PaymentsToAcquireBusinessesNetOfCashAcquired) and only for material acquisitions consolidated in a 10-K/10-Q. (3) No target-company identifier. The target is a free-text name in the 8-K; there is no CIK for a private target, so entity resolution must be done by NLP + fuzzy matching. (4) Materiality thresholds: Item 2.01 is only required for acquisitions of a 'significant amount of assets'; small bolt-on deals are legally omissible and frequently omitted. (5) Foreign private issuers are much weaker: they file 6-K instead of 8-K, 6-K has NO item taxonomy at all (no equivalent of Item 2.01), is furnished rather than filed, and content is whatever the home-market disclosure was - so Japanese issuers' M&A news arrives as an unstructured 6-K attachment, often a translated TDnet/press release. FPIs also file annually (20-F) rather than quarterly. (6) Full-text search starts 2001 and caps at 10,000 retrievable hits per query. (7) The full-text search API is undocumented (the official FAQ makes no mention of efts.sec.gov or any JSON API), so it is unsupported and can change without notice; unrecognised parameters return HTTP 500 or are silently ignored. (8) Rate limit 10 req/s and no CORS - all access must be server-side. (9) The SEC 'does not provide technical support for debugging scripted processes' and disclaims data accuracy; the Financial Statement Data Sets were re-processed in December 2024 and may contain extraction errors. (10) Timing lag: 8-K Item 1.01/2.01 is due within 4 business days, so EDGAR is a same-week not same-hour signal, and it is a DISCLOSURE source - by the time it appears the deal is signed or closed, which makes it good for market intelligence and comparables but late for origination. (11) Country of a filer is only a business/incorporation address code, and the full-text-search location filter does not work.
ma_relevance: WHO BOUGHT WHOM, WHEN: 8-K Item 2.01 (closing date = filing's reportDate; acquirer = the filer CIK, resolvable to name/ticker/SIC/address via the submissions API; target = free-text in the body) and 8-K Item 1.01 (signing date). Volume CONFIRMED: 1,107 documents in 2025 carry the exact Item 2.01 heading. For public-public deals the target also files - SC 14D9 (55 in 2025) or DEFM14A (235 in 2025) - giving both sides a CIK, and Form 15-12G (448 in 2025) marks the target's deregistration after closing. For merger-of-equals / stock deals: S-4 (391) and F-4 (73) name both parties and carry the exchange ratio; Form 425 (6,330) carries the deal press releases. For stake-building and activist/strategic pressure that precedes a deal: SCHEDULE 13D (11,274 including amendments in 2025) - Item 4 'Purpose of Transaction' states control intent, and the subject company is a separate CIK in the filing. DEAL VALUE: no structured field. Best-effort ladder - (1) EX-99.1 press release attached to the Item 1.01/2.01 8-K (headline enterprise value, per-share price); (2) EX-2.1 merger/purchase agreement (definitive consideration mechanics, escrow, earn-out); (3) DEFM14A / SC 14D9 (per-share consideration, premium, fairness opinion, DCF and comparable-company tables - the single richest free source of valuation multiples); (4) after closing, XBRL tags in the acquirer's 10-K/10-Q: BusinessCombinationConsiderationTransferred1, PaymentsToAcquireBusinessesNetOfCashAcquired, BusinessAcquisitionsProFormaRevenue, BusinessCombinationRecognizedIdentifiableAssetsAcquiredAndLiabilitiesAssumedNetGoodwill, Goodwill - retrievable per company via companyconcept or across all companies for a period via frames. FOR A JAPANESE ADVISORY FIRM specifically: (a) inbound - any US-listed acquirer buying a Japanese target must disclose it in an 8-K, giving a clean feed of US-buyer appetite for Japanese assets (search 8-K full text for 'Japan', 'Japanese', 'Kabushiki Kaisha', 'K.K.', 'Co., Ltd.'); (b) outbound - the ~1,000 Japan-addressed EDGAR filers plus Japanese 20-F issuers disclose their own acquisitions in 20-F business-combination notes and 6-K; (c) comparables and multiples for pitch books, free, including fairness-opinion methodology sections; (d) buyer-list building - SIC code plus acquisition history per CIK identifies serial acquirers in a target's sector.
implementation_notes: PIPELINE (all costs USD 0, only compute/storage). PHASE 1 - DAILY POLL: once per business day fetch https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/daily-index/{YYYY}/{QTRn}/form.{YYYYMMDD}.idx (1 request; the file is a fixed-width text list - form type in cols 1-12/14, CIK at col 75, accession path at the end). Filter to the M&A form set: 8-K, 8-K/A, S-4, S-4/A, F-4, DEFM14A, PREM14A, SC TO-T, SC TO-I, SC 14D9, SCHEDULE 13D, SCHEDULE 13D/A, 425, 15-12G, 10-12B, 6-K, 20-F. Expected daily yield (from 2025 annuals / 252 business days): ~270 8-K, ~110 6-K, ~1.5 S-4, ~9 SCHEDULE 13D-family, ~1 DEFM14A, ~25 Form 425 -> roughly 420 candidate filings/day. PHASE 2 - ITEM FILTER (cheap): for each candidate 8-K fetch {accession}-index-headers.html (~6 KB) and read the 'ITEM INFORMATION:' lines, keeping only 'Entry into a Material Definitive Agreement', 'Completion of Acquisition or Disposition of Assets', 'Changes in Control of Registrant', 'Termination of a Material Definitive Agreement'. Alternative with zero extra fetches for known-universe monitoring: pull https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK##########.json for a watchlist of CIKs and read filings.recent.items directly. PHASE 3 - DOCUMENT FETCH: for survivors fetch index.json for the accession, then the primary .htm plus any EX-2.1 (agreement) and EX-99.1/EX-99.x (press release). Surviving volume is small - only ~1,100 Item 2.01 documents in all of 2025. PHASE 4 - EXTRACT: LLM or regex extraction of target name, jurisdiction, consideration (cash/stock/mix, headline value, per-share price), expected/actual closing date, financing, advisors; then entity-resolve target names against JCAI's Salesforce Account/Target objects. PHASE 5 - ENRICH: acquirer profile from the submissions API (name, tickers, exchanges, sic/sicDescription, addresses, formerNames); post-deal purchase accounting from https://data.sec.gov/api/xbrl/companyconcept/CIK.../us-gaap/PaymentsToAcquireBusinessesNetOfCashAcquired.json. PHASE 6 - BACKFILL (2001 to date): use the full-text search API in slices, because of the 10,000-hit cap - loop over (form type x month), e.g. q=%22Completion%20of%20Acquisition%20or%20Disposition%20of%20Assets%22&forms=8-K&startdt=YYYY-MM-01&enddt=YYYY-MM-31, 100 hits per page via &from=0,100,...; read the exact total from aggregations.form_filter rather than hits.total when the latter says relation 'gte'. Also use q for Japan-specific screens ('Kabushiki Kaisha', 'Japan', 'Yen') to isolate Japan-touching deals. CALL BUDGET: at the mandated 10 req/s ceiling (use ~5 req/s to be safe) a 25-year backfill of ~30,000 Item-2.01 documents plus their exhibits (~90,000 requests) takes about 5 hours; steady-state daily operation is ~500-900 requests/day = under 3 minutes. STORAGE (INFERRED from measured samples): 8-K primary docs average ~40 KB, so all 67,651 of 2025's 8-Ks would be ~2.7 GB, but the M&A-filtered subset (Item 1.01 + 2.01 + their EX-2.1/EX-99.1) is well under 1 GB/year; a 2001-2026 M&A corpus is plausibly 10-25 GB of raw HTML, far less as extracted text. Bulk alternatives if per-request polling is unwelcome: submissions.zip (~1.46 GB, nightly) gives every filer's complete filing history including 8-K items offline in one download; companyfacts.zip (~1.31 GB, nightly) gives all XBRL facts; Financial Statement Data Sets are ~60-120 MB per quarter (2025Q3 ~122 MB) from 2009Q1, so roughly 4-6 GB for the full history. MANDATORY HYGIENE: send 'User-Agent: Japan Corporate Advisory Institute <contact email>' on every request, gzip Accept-Encoding, stay at or under 10 req/s, retry 429/503 with backoff, and never call data.sec.gov from browser JS (no CORS) - route through Apex/an integration user or a middleware service.
confidence: HIGH for everything marked CONFIRMED: API endpoints, JSON field names, rate limit, User-Agent requirement, archive windows, bulk ZIP byte sizes, 2025 filing volumes by form type and unique CIK, the 10,000-hit pagination cap, the full-text-search hit structure and aggregations, exhibit file_type values, SGML 'ITEM INFORMATION' availability, submissions-API 'items' field, XBRL frames datapoint counts, EDGAR country codes M0=Japan and U0=Singapore, 1,036 Japan-addressed filers, 10,391 tickered registrants. MEDIUM for the 20-F-by-country document counts (aggregation buckets are truncated to 30 and three buckets sat at exactly 100, and they count documents not filers) and for the L3/F5/K7/M5 country-code readings. LOW for the total FPI population by country - the SEC's own list is PDF-only and stale as of 2015-12-31, and the successor URL 404s. Volumes and sizes were measured on 2026-09-03 and will drift.
